rationale: The executable half of the contract, and the description VALUE (not the raw text). Six findings, all measured. (1) A field selection inside a fragment or an inline fragment targets `<Type>.<field>`, because the document itself states the type it is written against — `... on Admin { level }` is `Admin.level`, and `fragment UserFields on User { id }` is `User.id`. Both resolve to an SDL property; the pre-fix bare targets resolved to nothing. (2) An ALIAS is not the fact: `nick: name` references `name`. (3) A VARIABLE REFERENCE is a fact: `user(id: $id)` and `@include(if: $withPosts)` are uses-edges from the operation to `$id` / `$withPosts`. The pre-fix analyzer declared both variables and recorded no use of either, so every variable in a real query read as dead. (4) A description is a VALUE: `"` and `\` are resolved, and a block string is dedented per §2.9.4. The pre-fix implementation returned the raw inner text with its backslashes intact, published `a \"quote\"` where the source says `a "quote"`, and left a block description's common indent and its blank lines in place. (5) `isOptional` follows GraphQL's own rule — an argument is optional only when it is NULLABLE *and* has a default. The pre-fix asked only whether the type carried `!`, so it reported both nullable shapes as optional and inverted the one distinction the specification makes. (6) A directive applied to a selection is a real reference to the `@directive` function symbol, and a directive on an enum value is a real reference too; the pre-fix analyzer dropped both, and Apollo Federation's `@key`/`@external`/`@requires` are the whole structure of a federated subgraph. Also pinned: a fragment spread and an inline fragment's type condition are uses-edges, and the nested selections of a FIELD are bare, because inside a field's own selection set the parent type is the field's return type and an executable document does not carry it. Every executable relationship carries `meta.selectionPath`, and the fixture pins it, so 'qualified where the document states the type, bare where it does not' is an assertion and not a description: `User.id` at path `id` (the fragment's own root) and bare `id` at path `user.posts.edges.node.id` are the same fixture, and only the path tells them apart. (7) Ledger rule R9: the positions where a DECLARATION writes a type name are `references` carrying metadata.relationshipType='declared_type', not `uses` — and two `forbidRelationships` rows pin the old label so a reversion is caught rather than tolerated. (8) `exports` is published as an EDGE as well as ExportInfo, because nothing in the product reads ParseResult.exports; three rows here and the census's 1,428 over 426 corpus files.
